$sources: The rocks: scholar's rocks (gongshi) are limestones worn by water; Taihu stone from Lake Tai (Jiangsu) is dissolved by water into cavities and perforations, Lingbi stone (Anhui) is dark and resonant; they are prized for thinness (shou), openness (tou), perforation (lou) and wrinkling (zhou), and shown on a wooden stand carved for the stone (Wikipedia, 'Scholar's rock', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scholar%27s_rock ; 'Taihu stone', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taihu_stone : 'due to long-term surging by water, this kind of stone features pores and holes'; read 2026-09-27). Docs/Matter's Palette.json accent.taihu-rock and accent.lingbi-rock name their stone.

The Taihu kind: the as-built museum's standing rock (windows/Source/MuseeVision/Nature/MuseeTaihuRock.cpp, after Shared/Wings/ChineseWing.swift: 'tall, waisted, twin-peaked, pitted'): its north-south silhouette 2.0 m across at the foot, 1.48 at 0.93 m, 1.84 at 1.77 m, waisted to 1.08 at 2.52 m, 1.52 at 3.27 m, and two peaks at 4.08 and 4.20 m over a saddle at 3.78 m, taken here as shares of its height and widest; four through-holes and about nine more at full erosion, 0.08 to 0.20 m in radius on a rock 4.1 m high; about 55 pits 0.05 to 0.17 m in radius; wrinkles about 0.09 m deep; its form bent by up to 0.14 m; cells of 0.04 m.

The Lingbi kind: Chenghuai's sheet (Docs/Stages/chenghuai.md, section 8): a Lingbi rock 0.32 high on the painting table, on a carved phoebe stand r 0.11 x 0.03 that the stage draws (linquan.table.rock-stand). Its form is a design value after the type: a compact small mountain, grooved up its height and pitted, with few holes through, a little wider at its shoulders than its foot and three peaks along its top.

Each rock's foot: 石兄's base keeps within r 0.60 of its centre, the path dividing round it at r 1.475 (chenghuai.md, section 3.9 and Build notes item 8); the Lingbi rock's foot within its stand's r 0.11.
